thread:
sam: i ran into a reproducible demote race this morning when a tenant hotkey moved between shards. thinking about a lightweight logical-clock approach to order demote/rehydrate actions across nodes.
maria: can you sketch the problem? i skimmed logs but lost the sequence.
ajay: yes pls — i want to see how this compares to the lease/version hacks we've used.
sam: short version: NodeA demotes prefix P at clock 42, NodeB concurrently rehydrates at clock 41 because it saw a stale handoff ack. result: NodeB serves stale entries, then NodeA later tries to reclaim and tombstones things, breaking read-after-write for in-flight ops.
linh: ugh. that's the classic clock-skew+async-handoff issue. currently we rely on lease heartbeats to reduce it, but that adds latency and complexity.
sam: proposal: attach a cheap, monotonic "demote_clock" per-prefix. Any demote or rehydrate carries the clock; nodes accept only ops with clock >= local_seen_clock for that prefix. we advance clocks on handoff completion and on explicit demote.
maria: sounds like vector clocks but one number per-prefix. how do we avoid a single slow node pinning the clock?
ajay: you don't need global coordination. the demote action that completes (handoff ack path) returns a new clock value (local monotonic counter + wall-time tie-breaker). it's advisory: receivers adopt max(local, incoming).
ben: how would this look in code? quick pseudo:

```
// on demote request
local_clock = read_counter(prefix)
candidate = local_clock + 1
send demote(prefix, candidate)
// on demote ack
write_counter(prefix, max(read_counter(prefix), candidate))

// on incoming rehydrate/demote
if incoming.clock < read_counter(prefix): reject_or_retry()
else accept()
```

linh: rejecting on lower clock is interesting — does that cause retries or fail-fast? for client-facing reads we should prefer fail-open.
sam: agree. for user-read paths we can accept and mark as "stale_possible" and trigger background verification. for mutation or handoff control ops we should require clock >= local.
olga: what about cross-prefix operations (multi-prefix transactions)?
maria: multi-prefix would need to snapshot clocks, but that's already tricky. for now keep this protocol limited to single-prefix cache demote/rehydrate actions.
ajay: what about persistence? counters need to survive restarts to avoid regressions.
sam: counters are tiny (one int per prefix) — we persist to local metadata store and replicate via the usual raft/log replication used for shard metadata. on node failure we can accept lower clocks temporarily but the reclaim path will re-increment.
ben: telemetry idea: emit "demote_clock_gap" whenever incoming.clock < local_clock by more than N. helps catch clients behind.
linh: edge case: network partition where two nodes both advance the clock independently and then reconnect — both will propose different candidates; max-on-write reconciles, right?
sam: yes, because recipients write max(local, incoming). clocks are monotonic and converge by max. tie on same int use node-id or wall-time.
maria: do we need a GC or compaction for these counters? some prefixes are ephemeral.
sam: TTL the metadata for prefixes that haven't been seen in X days. small overhead.
deploy-bot: deploy plan suggestion: rollout feature-flagged; start with telemetry-only for 2 weeks; then opt-in tenants; finally global flip.
ajay: +1 on opt-in. we should also add integration test that simulates async handoff with clock skew.
olga: one more thought: document the failure semantics clearly — "lower-clock acceptance = potential stale read, not data loss". ops teams will want this spelled out.
sam: good call. i'll draft an RFC with pseudocode, test plan, and rollout schedule. for now i'm enabling telemetry-only locally and will post logs.
maria: thanks Sam. assign an owner for the RFC? (cc @ajay)
ajay: i'll own the RFC writeup with Sam. will start a PR by EOD.
sam: thanks — i'll drop a short reproducer and a mini-sim in the PR. :thumbsup:
